summary: Bob and his allies face a large gorilloid assault on the Deltan colony. The Deltans defend Archimedes with spears and a hand axe, while Bob directs a buster drone to stop a breakthrough. The battle leaves heavy Deltan losses and raises concern about recoverable technological wreckage. As the group considers returning the Deltans to their former flint site, Luke and Bender decide to seek projects elsewhere while Marvin stays involved with the Deltans.

introducing.name: hand axe
introducing.description: A large hand axe made by Archimedes for Deltan defense. Comparable in scale to a felling axe, it proves effective against gorilloids and becomes a model the other Deltan males want to reproduce.

introducing.name: Battle at the Deltan colony
introducing.description: A large gorilloid assault on the Deltan colony kills thirty Deltans and injures about fifteen more. The Deltans repel the attackers with their weapons and Bob's buster-drone intervention, but the losses deepen the danger facing their small community.

updates.description: An interface that offloads tasks for replicants while retaining their human limits on multitasking. Its name expands to General Unit Primary Peripheral Interface, and its logs retain monitoring-interface and script activity. Its operating system is firmware; changing its replication priority would require a new core and ship. Version-2 GUPPI is being given enough memory capacity that a personality matrix is contemplated. It can take messages and arrange callbacks for Riker, acting as a secretary and receptionist. It can estimate buster-drone deployment time and launch buster drones on Bob's order.

A buster drone is an observation drone reinforced internally and fitted with steel impact caps. It can strike with forty pounds of high-tensile steel at twice the speed of a high-powered rifle bullet, delivering a lethal kinetic blow and sonic boom against a gorilloid. Atmospheric entry requires a controlled descent, so a deployment can take about ten minutes to reach a surface target.

A practical drone design for planetary exploration, with variants for surveillance and biological analysis. The football-sized surveillance variant has remote cameras, microphones, extendable gripping limbs, and small shielded reactors that can detect incoming craft before detection. It can relay live video, record speech, and provide footage for a virtual-reality reconstruction of observed inhabitants. Observation drones cannot quickly accelerate because they lack legs. The roughly meter-long biological-analysis variant has visual and auditory input optimized for close work and many extendable appendages for varied tasks; it also carries systems for examining local life and mechanical stomachs that process organics as a human stomach would, with sample-output analysis taking about a day. The drones can change color with limited pattern mimicry.
